name: SE Mega Slab
itinerary: Day 1: Drive to Salmon La Sac Trailhead and hike the Waptus River Trail to Waptus Lake, then the PCT south to a camp at the bridge over the Waptus River. Day 2: Follow the unmaintained path along Shovel Creek to the base of the Mega Slab (~4.5 hrs from the vehicle), climb the ~3,000-ft slab to the south shoulder (~80 min) and the ~600-ft summit block scramble to the top, then descend to Shovel Lake (~1.5 hrs) and return to camp. Day 3: Hike back out to the trailhead.

pitch_detail.notes: ~3,000 vertical ft of continuous sandstone slab from ~3,700 ft at Shovel Creek to the ~6,700 ft south shoulder; climbed in trail runners with minimal hand use, roughly 80 minutes in one trip report.
~600 ft above the slab; traverse the west side via exposed scrambling and heather benches.
Short, easy-but-exposed final pitch on loose rock to the true summit, including a short chimney section; one party soloed it though they carried a rope.

pro_tips: Approach shoes or trail runners work well on the clean sandstone friction slab
Camp at the PCT bridge over the Waptus River to break the long approach into two days
The slab itself takes roughly 80 minutes to reach the south shoulder once you're on it
Only a handful of parties climb this line per year — expect no beta cairns or fixed anchors
